chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the man who leaves his house intending to travel while he is fasting, so he (peace be upon him) said:
He said: If he leaves before the middle of the day, let him break his fast and make up for that day; and if he leaves after the decline (of the sun), let him complete his day.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking a fast if one intends to travel during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the critical criterion of 'intention' (niyyah) timing relative to zawal (noon) for travelers in Ramadan, a foundational principle in Shia fiqh for determining fast validity. It highlights the juristic distinction that breaking the fast is obligatory if the decision to travel occurs before midday, whereas maintaining the fast is required if the intention arises after, reflecting the practical application of ease in Islamic law.
